children: RIIL share price, Oct. 7 -- Shares of Reliance Industrial Infrastructure (RIIL) surged almost 9% in morning trade on the BSE on Wednesday, 7 October, defying weak stock market sentiment. Reliance Industrial Infra share price opened at Rs.682 against its previous close of Rs.680.55 and jumped as much as 8.7% to an intraday high of Rs.740, looking set to extend gains for the second consecutive session. On the other hand, equity benchmark Sensex declined by 0.75% during the session.
The stock surged on Wednesday, with trading volume more than 5 times higher.

The stock is down 13% year-to-date, largely in sync with a 14% decline in the equity benchmark Sensex. It hit a 52-week high of Rs.963.65 on 8 October last year and a 52-week low of Rs.620.50 on 30 March this year.
On a monthly scale, the stock is up 6% so far in October after a 10% decline in September.

On 15 July, RIIL said its total income declined 18.4% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs.14.92 crore in Q1FY27 from Rs.18.28 crore for the same period, following the completion of certain fixed-term contracts. Net profit for the quarter declined 8.4% YoY to Rs.2.84 crore from Rs.3.10 crore in the same quarter last year.

According to Aditya Thukral, founder and analyst at AT Research and Risk Managers, Reliance Industrial Infrastructure has been in a corrective mode since the formation of multi-year highs in January 2024.
The correction seems to be still ongoing, and the prices are expected to approach fresh 52-week lows in the months to come.

"All the rallies will continue to get sold off till the time another leg of correction is completed on the downside. The stock is trading below all the major EMAs and is now approaching a resistance zone, which could be an exit opportunity for longs," said Thukral.

"The stock is in corrective mode, which is expected to continue for some more months before the stock can find a bottom. Existing investors should try to exit near the resistance zone of Rs.720 to Rs.780. Fresh longs should only be executed once we start getting clues of completion of the correction," said Thukral.
